prompt:
Generate exactly FIVE separate widescreen 16:9 frames from one restrained live-action historical feature film set in a poor Caribbean merchant port in 1772. Deliver five independent image files, one image per scene, in the order below. Do not make a contact sheet, collage, split screen, storyboard layout, variations of one scene, captions or frame numbers.

CAST LOCK FOR IMAGES 1, 2, 3, 5: The protagonist is a fictional SEVENTEEN-YEAR-OLD YOUNG MAN who has reached his adult height, about 173 cm. Adult-length arms and legs, a narrow angular face, prominent straight nose, defined jaw, lean and underfed rather than muscular. He must visibly be several years past childhood. Light olive skin with sun exposure and small natural blemishes, deep brown eyes. His dark brown wavy hair is grown below the collar and gathered in a clearly visible LOW PONYTAIL at the nape, tied with a small plain dark cloth strip. Hair swept back off his forehead, a few untidy strands at his temples. Clean-shaven. He has the unpolished presence of a young Caribbean-born clerk in the 1770s. Keep the same face, hairline, ponytail, proportions and clothes in all four images. No bowl cut, no straight fringe, no cropped schoolboy haircut, no baby face, no child-size body, no glamorous actor grooming.

His clothing is practical 1770s working clothing: coarse off-white linen shirt with a short standing neckband and an open slit at the throat, rumpled sleeves rolled to forearms; long plain faded charcoal-brown waistcoat reaching the hips, hand-sewn edges; worn brown KNEE BREECHES ending just below the knees; dull gray-beige stockings visibly continuing below the breeches; plain worn brown leather shoes. No modern trousers, shirt collars, zippers, metal backpack fittings, lace ruffles or pirate costume. Do not use the appearance of a real actor or celebrity.

PHOTOGRAPHY: A physical movie camera at ordinary human height in a cramped real location. Neutral, irregular natural daylight, exposed humid skin and linen textures, worn but useful objects, patchy limewash, damp marks and tropical greenery beyond windows. Modest dynamic range with bright exteriors and dim interiors. Imperfect mundane framing, objects cut by the edge because the room is cramped. Skin is not retouched. No portrait sitting, looking at camera, theatrical staging, golden grading, chiaroscuro painting, decorative haze, shallow focus spectacle or heroic posing. These are work interrupted by a camera, not publicity stills. Keep contact between hands and objects anatomically convincing. No modern plumbing, electric fixtures, glass screw-top bottles, factory paper printouts or legible captions.

ROOM B, used in images 1 and 2: cramped limewashed room; rough small writing table directly below a rectangular blue-green painted wooden shutter window. The two old shutter leaves are hinged at the two OUTER sides of the window frame. The LEFT leaf has a small irregular gap where two slats are broken in its lower third; the RIGHT leaf is intact and has a broad horizontal solid wooden brace at the man's chest height. There is a dark damp patch in the lower right wall corner. Same window proportions, same damaged slats, same walls, same small table. The table's inner left corner is dry, its strip next to the window wet. No glass pane, no taps or pipes.

IMAGE 1 — WRITING AFTER THE STORM (later identified as S05): Establish the young man's recognizable face here. A medium shot from his left side and slightly behind his shoulder, showing his angular cheek and nose in natural profile, tied long hair clearly visible at the nape, both hands and part of the desk. He is seated in room B. Outside, a broken banana leaf and battered vegetation are bright under overcast daylight after rain. Shutters are open; their exact damaged left leaf remains visible. His right hand holds a simple real cut goose quill directly by its bare narrow shaft, with no modern pen attached. Its point is resting at the last small stroke of the last word. His left hand rests on the near corner of one small OFF-WHITE ROUGH RAG PAPER sheet. In its upper middle are FOUR SHORT LINES of very SMALL fine brown-black cursive handwriting: varied loops, ascenders and descenders, natural word spaces, modest uneven line ends. It should look like a real person's letter at this distance, too small and oblique to read the exact sentence. The lower half of the sheet is mostly unmarked. No tally strokes, oversized pseudo-letters, repeated symbols or sheet filled edge-to-edge. A thumb-sized dark unglazed earthenware inkpot with a simple open lip stands beyond the paper. His attention is on the final word; a quiet concentrated working posture. Leave enough of the window and damp wall to establish the physical room; do not make the paper a close-up.

IMAGE 2 — HOLDING THE SHUTTER DURING THE STORM (S04): Same seventeen-year-old young man, visibly the SAME LOW PONYTAIL and same adult proportions and clothes as image 1. Same room B, earlier in the storm. Medium rear-side view; his head and hands below the upper third of frame. The two shutters are now ALMOST CLOSED into the same window opening, with only a narrow vertical gap between them. The recognizable broken lower slats remain in the left leaf. Both palms are ALREADY FLAT against solid wood on the right leaf at chest height, one a little lower, fingers spread naturally. He leans his body weight forward with elbows bent and shoulders rounded, quietly resisting the wind pushing the shutter inward. Neither arm is overhead, neither hand hangs in empty air, he is not lifting a loose plank or operating a latch. Side rain and dark gray daylight appear through the small gap. The near edge of the same table is visible below his forearms. No flood spectacle or flying debris.

IMAGE 3 — KEEPING THE MERCHANT'S ACCOUNTS DRY (S03): Same seventeen-year-old young man and clear long low ponytail, left shoulder rear medium shot in a working small merchant storeroom. He already holds a closed worn leather ledger in both hands just above a dry shelf, ready to lay it down. A dry shelf surface is clearly visible directly BELOW the ledger, unobstructed. A couple of wrapped parcels and another book on an adjacent shelf, one open doorway reveals an ordinary wooden barrel and a distant worker in plain period clothing. The room has old irregular plank walls with patched limewash, a rope coil hanging from a wooden peg, old worn dry and wet areas on the floor. Dampness is explained only by a few roof drips falling from the upper edge of frame onto an empty wooden bucket well to the side. NO METAL WATER TAP, NO FAUCET, NO PIPES, no indoor sink. Room retains useful everyday disorder. The person is occupied with the ledger, no turn to camera.

TRAVEL BAG LOCK FOR IMAGES 4 AND 5: a SMALL slack gray-brown coarse linen drawstring sack, approximately 30 cm tall, with one dark charcoal-brown near-circular CLOTH patch hand-stitched low on its front. A SINGLE LONG WIDE GRAY-BROWN CLOTH SHOULDER STRAP. It is a modest soft sack that fits a change of shirt, not a huge stuffed modern hiking backpack. No second shoulder strap, buckles, leather hardware or logo. Keep exactly this cloth, patch position, size and strap in both images.

IMAGE 4 — A READER SETS ASIDE THE FARE (S06): A different man, a weathered fifty-year-old local merchant in plain working linen and an old brown waistcoat, sits behind an unvarnished table. Medium side view, composed around his working hands, with his head near the upper edge and gaze lowered, not a formal portrait. His LEFT hand holds one rough folded letter upright with the UNWRITTEN REVERSE facing the camera, a faint trace of tiny ink may show through but no visible text columns. His RIGHT hand already rests on a small tied dark leather COIN POUCH on his side of the tabletop, about to slide it toward the travel bag. Both hands and their separate objects clearly visible. The modest linen travel bag described above rests at the front-left of the table, patch and single loose shoulder strap visible, beside a folded old coat. A short unobstructed tabletop path leads from his right hand's coin pouch to the travel bag. No coins spread out, no smiling agreement, no second person. The shot quietly links the letter and money to preparations for a journey.

IMAGE 5 — ONE STEP ABOARD (S07): Same seventeen-year-old young man with the SAME long low ponytail and period knee breeches with stockings, carrying the SAME SMALL cloth travel sack from image 4 against his left hip, its single wide strap running diagonally across his shoulder and torso. The patch faces the camera. Fixed camera on shore at waist height, several meters behind and to his right, a FULL-BODY medium-wide shot that includes BOTH SHOES AND ALL OF THE SHORT GANGPLANK. He faces diagonally AWAY from the camera TOWARD THE BOAT. One shoe is already planted securely on the lowest plank, the other shoe is still on the stone quay. His hands hang down naturally, eyes toward his footing, no looking back. A short rough ramp with cross battens spans a SMALL GAP from the quay up to a CLEAR OPENING in the LOW GUNWALE of an ordinary moored coastal cargo vessel. Both ends of the ramp rest on solid supports; the opening and the small patch of deck beyond it are unobstructed and visibly reachable. Only the NEAR HULL, gunwale opening and small section of deck appear; crop the rest of the boat outside the frame. No giant sailing ship seen in full, no towering pirate galleon, no display of masts or vast rigging, no grand harbor panorama. A little blue-green water at the edge, damp pale stone quay, one rough wooden barrel, distant low plaster port buildings. Mundane daylight, a practical departure, no sunset symbolism.

Final check: exactly five separate photographs in this order. Image 1 establishes a nearly grown young man, NOT A CHILD. Images 2, 3, 5 retain his adult proportions and clearly tied long hair. Images 1/2 share the same room and shutter damage. Images 4/5 share the same small single-strap bag. Each image is one continuous plausible photographic space, not an illustrated scene.
